The Raku ecosystem under Raku++

Every distribution in the REA index — latest release of each — fetched, built, installed and its own test suite run under Raku++.

Measured 2026-08-30 on Raku++ v3.23.0-8-g5e23726, against Rakudo 2026.08 as the oracle.

1006 of 2,529 distributions pass their own tests. A verdict names the first rung that failed, so a fix tends to move a dist one rung: pass passes its own test suite · build-fail its native build step fails · dep-build-fail a dependency’s build fails · dep-fail a dependency fails first · fetch-fail could not be fetched · other exited abnormally · self-fail its own suite fails · timeout ran past its time budget. The sweep, the fix campaign it drove, and the per-dist raw results live in the write-up; the trend is on the dashboard. Two badges sit outside the ladder, because the frontend decides them, not us: legacy is a dist riding the pre-RakuAST frontend — an old slang hook, QAST, P5tie — which stops working on stock Rakudo at 6.e whatever we do, so it is never charged to the engine (27); needs-AST is a dist using the RakuAST API, blocked on Raku++ rather than on its author (20). A badge is independent of the verdict — P5tie is green and legacy — so the two chip rows filter independently. The table opens most-depended-on first; click a header to re-sort, and the filter matches distribution names, authors, and the dependencies a dist is blocked by alike.

234 distributions never reach their own test suite because something in their dependency chain fails first, and 0 of those wait on more than one — a row opens to show every dependency it is stuck behind, with that dependency’s own error. Between them they wait on 169 distinct distributions. The ones the most dists wait on:  14 ·  5 ·  5 ·  5 ·  4 ·  4 ·  3 ·  3.
